### F841

| Status | Class | Sev | Issue | Evidence | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| FIXED F841 | DEFECT | low | A polled io_uring transfer used to run INLINE and post its completion before anything could poll for it, so `IORING_ENTER_GETEVENTS` returned from the precheck and the poll loop never ran. Closed by building the missing mechanism rather than arguing the premise: `FileOps::submit_direct` (`vfs::file_ops::DirectIo`/`DirectSubmit`) is the reference's `-EIOCBQUEUED` arm, the block bridge implements it over `BlockDevice::submit`'s existing owned-request completion, and a transfer on a polled ring is now SUBMIT-THEN-POLL: prepared in the submitter (segments imported, write payload gathered), issued to the backend, and left with NO CQE until `io_uring_enter(GETEVENTS)` drives the poll and reaps it. The request is held by a STRONG `ctx->iopoll_list` on the ring, because nothing else holds a transfer the backend owns; the backend's completion owns only the result slot, never the request or user memory, so it is safe from any context and after the ring is gone. Exactly-once completion goes through the existing `IoReq::claim`. A read's bytes are scattered into the SUBMITTER's address space by page-table root, not through whichever task reaps. | F841. Hosted: `block::devbridge::tests::a_queued_direct_read_returns_without_completing` (submitted, `slot` still empty, device holds it, only `iopoll` completes it), `a_queued_direct_write_lands_and_a_later_read_sees_it`, `f_op_submit_direct_on_an_open_block_description_reaches_the_driver`; `block::direct::plan` (9 tests). Positive control: making the fixture's `submit` complete inline turned exactly those 3 deferral tests RED; restored GREEN. | — |
| FIXED F841 | MISSING | low | `IORING_SETUP_HYBRID_IOPOLL` is implemented. The estimate it sleeps against is the ring's own running MINIMUM of observed service times — the reference's `ctx->hybrid_poll_time`, not a block-layer statistic, which is what the old refusal got wrong about where the number lives. A queued transfer is stamped at issue, each poll pass sleeps for half the current estimate before polling (once per transfer, never once per pass), and folds `now - issued_at - slept` back in as a minimum. Minimum rather than average for the reference's stated reason: with backends of different speeds, sleeping longer than the fastest takes loses completions that were ready. | F841. `io_uring_abi::iopoll::{hybrid_sleep_ns,observe_runtime,hybrid_runtime}` + 6 hosted tests, including one that feeds the estimate through its own sleep 8 times and asserts it does not ratchet. `layout/tests.rs::every_setup_flag_is_either_implemented_or_refused` now records it as implemented and fails if it regresses. | — |

| FIXED F850 | MISSING | MED | **An `SK_REUSEPORT` program can now NAME a member.** `BPF_MAP_TYPE_REUSEPORT_SOCKARRAY` and `bpf_sk_select_reuseport` (helper 82) both exist and are wired: a program stores socket descriptors into the map from userspace, names a slot at run time, and the named socket becomes the index the arriving packet is handed to. | FIXED B2255 | DEFECT | high | **The serial-sysrq armed state never expired, so a single stray NUL on the console armed it forever and the next character to arrive ran a sysrq command — including `c` (crash) and `b` (reboot).** `SYSRQ_ARMED` was a bare `AtomicBool` set by the break and cleared only by the next received byte, and our boot line forces the mask to enable-all, so line noise that happened to deliver a zero byte left the machine one keystroke from a deliberate panic with nothing in the log to explain the reboot. The armed state is now the DEADLINE the line is armed until, in one word as the reference keeps it, with `DISARMED = 0` as the sentinel; every dispatch is gated on the current time still being before it and every path out of an armed line clears it. Window: five seconds, the reference's `HZ * 5`. Clock: `timekeeper::monotonic_ns`, a lock-free seqlock read over the architecture counter documented safe from hard IRQ (its writers mask interrupts) — chosen over a tick counter deliberately, because this kernel's tick freezes for seconds under an I/O storm and a tick-derived deadline would then outlive its own window. | B2255. Reference 7.2-rc4: `SYSRQ_TIMEOUT` is `HZ * 5`; the break handler stores `jiffies + SYSRQ_TIMEOUT`; both `uart_handle_sysrq_char` and `uart_prepare_sysrq_char` dispatch only under `ch && time_before(jiffies, port->sysrq)` and clear the field otherwise. | FIXED F1223 | MISSING | high | **A `MAP_SHARED` writable mmap of an f2fs file does not write through to the file, and the two WRITE-side mapped iostat rows (`app mapped data`, `app mapped cdata` under `[WRITE]`) therefore still read zero.** `F2fsMapping::shared_frame` answers `None` because an f2fs data page is held as a `Vec<u8>` inside `block::pagecache`, which is heap memory a user page table cannot point at. With `None`, `mm-vmm/src/address_space/fault/fill.rs:172` and `fault/write.rs:145` both fall to the private read-copy COW path, so a store into a shared mapping lands in a per-mapping copy that no flush ever reaches — silent loss of an `msync`'d write, and no fault the filesystem can charge. **Precise diagnosis, so the next lane does not re-derive it.** Closing this is the D8 project ext4 already went through, and it is TWO pieces, in this order: (1) f2fs data pages must BE machine frames, i.e. a per-mount frame store (`pmm::setup::alloc_object_frame` + `frame_ptr` + `inc_ref`, mapped as `VmaBacking::KernelFrame` and never `PhysRange`) that the plain arms of `volume/io.rs` and `volume/fileops.rs` read and patch, replacing the byte vector rather than sitting beside it — a frame store ADDED beside the existing `Vec` cache is the split source of truth this project forbids, and was the reason F1211 stopped here rather than shipping half of it; ext4's equivalent is `ext4/src/rootfs/framecache.rs` plus nine child modules, and f2fs would additionally need `pmm` and `hal` dependencies it does not have today. (2) The reference's `page_mkwrite` has no counterpart in this kernel at all: `vm_operations_struct.page_mkwrite` is where f2fs allocates the block, takes the quota, zeroes the post-EOF tail, dirties the folio and charges `APP_MAPPED_IO`, and our fault paths call only `shared_frame`, which cannot distinguish a read fault from a write fault. That needs an `AddressSpaceOps::page_mkwrite(off)` (default no-op), a `FileBacking` forwarder, and a call from the two write-fault arms — a `vfs` + `mm-vmm` surface addition, Linux-shaped, but a boot-path one. | F1211. `mount/mapping.rs::shared_frame` returns `Ok(None)` with the reason in its doc comment; `f2fs/Cargo.toml` has no `pmm`/`hal` dependency; `grep -rn page_mkwrite crates/kernel/` returns nothing. The two WRITE rows are asserted at `(0, 0)` nowhere — they simply have no site, which is what this row is. **F1223.** A cached page is now a `PageBuf` (`block/src/pagecache/store.rs`): a heap buffer while nothing maps it, and the machine frame the bytes were MOVED into once something does, converted in place and one-way so a page never holds two copies. The frame allocator is named to the page cache by an installed provider (`pmm/src/setup/pagecache_frames.rs`, installed from `init_from_boot_info`), which is the same inversion `install_totalram_pages` already goes through — `pmm` depends on `block`, so the page cache cannot call the allocator directly. `AddressSpaceOps::page_mkwrite` / `FileOps::mmap_page_mkwrite` / `FileBacking::page_mkwrite` are new and called from BOTH write-fault arms (`mm-vmm .../fault/fill.rs::handle_not_present`, `.../fault/write.rs::handle_write_protection`) before the frame is asked for, because for a file on a medium that call is what reserves the block the frame will hold. f2fs implements it in `volume/mkwrite.rs` with the reference's ladder. Reachability: fault -> `InodeFileBacking::page_mkwrite` (`syscalls/src/mmap_file.rs`) -> `Inode::mmap_page_mkwrite` -> `F2fsMapping::page_mkwrite`. Decisive test `volume::mkwrite::tests::a_store_through_the_mapping_survives_a_flush_and_a_remount` writes through the frame, flushes as an `msync` does, and reads the bytes back from a filesystem mounted FRESH over the device. Positive controls: restoring `shared_frame -> Ok(None)` reddens 9 of 14; dropping the dirty mark reddens 3; dropping the reservation reddens the block-charge test. f2fs 3590 pass (was 3576), block 255 (was 244). | unowned |

| FIXED F1224 | DEFECT | high | **f2fs frees an unlinked file's inode IMMEDIATELY even while a handle is open, because the orphan machinery's "is it open" input has no caller on the open path.** `drop_last_link` parks the inode only `if self.inode_is_open(ino)`, and `open_inode` is called from exactly ONE place in the tree — the atomic-write COW setup (`atomic/start.rs:114`). So an ordinary `open` records no hold, and `unlink` of an open file runs `free_inode` and releases its blocks under the reader. The reference never frees at unlink: `f2fs_drop_nlink` adds the inode to the orphan list whenever `i_nlink` reaches zero, and the blocks are released in `f2fs_evict_inode` at the last reference. With `evict_inode` now wired (row above) the Linux shape is reachable: always park at `drop_last_link`, free at eviction. Not attempted here — it changes the unlink lifecycle every existing f2fs test asserts against, which is a lane of its own, not a rename/tmpfile edit. **FIXED F1224.** Losing a name now PARKS unconditionally (`drop_nlink`) and the eviction frees; the open-count gate and the count itself are gone — it was a second answer to "is anything using this file" beside the reference the layer above holds. Three further links of the chain were missing and were wired in the same PR, without which the parking is unreachable and an unlink LEAKS instead: the filesystem held no `Weak<SuperBlock>` (`set_sb` was unimplemented, so nothing could reach the inode cache); `node_inode` minted a FRESH in-core inode per lookup and never touched the cache, so an inode number named no single object, no reference count could reach zero and `evict_inode` was dead from the production path; and the cached link count was floored at one and never lowered on removal, so `drop_inode` read a link-less file as linked. Directories take the same path (rmdir parks, eviction frees, `i_size` truncated as it goes), a rename onto an existing name settles the inode it replaced the same way, and the list slot is reserved BEFORE the entry comes out so a full list refuses with the name intact. | F1217. `volume/orphan/list.rs:107` `drop_last_link`; the only `open_inode` caller outside tests is `atomic/start.rs:114`. Fix `52db8a23d`. Named call sites: `syscalls/src/087_unlink.rs:93` -> `vfs::inode::ops::unlink_child` -> `f2fs mount/ops.rs::unlink` -> `mount/write.rs::remove` -> `Volume::remove`/`drop_nlink` (parks) + `mount/evict.rs::after_remove`; and `vfs::file::lifetime::iput` -> `vfs superblock/icache.rs:104` -> `mount/sb.rs::evict_inode` -> `Volume::evict_inode` (frees). Tests: 4 in `f2fs/src/tests/orphan/unlinked_open.rs` driving `unlink_child`/`iput` end to end (read through a handle held across the unlink; last-reference free; the victim's block not reallocated while the handle lives; a name arriving first saves the file), plus rewritten `tests/orphan/live.rs`. Positive controls, each RED then GREEN: parking replaced by a free; the `evict_inode` hook gated off; the inode built with no superblock; the icache bypassed; `after_remove` not called; the reservation removed; the nlink floor restored. f2fs 3595 -> 3608, 0 failed; vfs 1912 and fs 1984 unchanged. | F1224 |

| FIXED B2249 | DEFECT | high | **The three ACPI IOMMU table parsers each reserved a 45-47 KB stack frame — nearly three times the whole 16 KiB kernel stack — on both arches.** `IommuInventory` is a ~24 KiB aggregate of fixed arrays (`[DmarRmrr; 32]` alone is 11776 B) and it was built as a stack local in `parse_dmar`/`parse_ivrs` and returned BY VALUE into `decode`'s frame, so the caller carried a second copy. Any DMAR or IVRS table on a real machine ran that. The reference does not hold a firmware table as one stack-resident aggregate: each translation unit is its own heap object linked into a global list, and the AMD side allocates its per-segment tables. Fixed by making the inventory heap-resident (`IommuInventory::boxed`, one copy from a `const EMPTY` in read-only data) and splitting the table walks into `fill_dmar`/`fill_ivrs` that take `&mut IommuInventory`, so the walk's frame holds a pointer instead of the table; `publish` takes `&IommuInventory` rather than a by-value copy. | B2249. Measured with `tools/frame-size-gate.py`, same tool both sides. Before: x86_64 `decode` 47384 / `parse_dmar` 45448 / `parse_ivrs` 44904; aarch64 46976 / 46320 / 46256. After: x86_64 440 / 456 / 40; aarch64 32 / 528 / 96. `cargo test -p firmware` 118 passed. |
| FIXED B2249 | COVERAGE | high | **The frame gate could not see a large x86_64 frame, for the same reason it could not see a large aarch64 one before B2248.** Past a threshold LLVM stops unrolling stack-clash probes and emits a LOOP: the whole reservation is subtracted from a COPY of `%rsp`, and the only `sub …,%rsp` in the prologue is the one-page loop body. Summing `sub …,%rsp` alone therefore read a 45448-byte frame as 4488. All three 45 KB ACPI frames above scored 4488, 6424 and 8040 — under or barely at the 8192 ceiling — so the gate reported the x86 binary as having one offender when it had four. Fixed by decoding the loop form (count the `sub` against the copy plus the sub-page tail, skip the loop body) with two self-test cases: the loop form, and a control where a `mov %rsp,%reg` that is not a probe setup must not swallow the following ordinary reservation. | B2249.
